justification: Item 6 asked what populates v2_extracted_rules and whether run_numeric_extraction is fixable or should be deleted. Answered: enrichment/rule_extraction_pipeline.py populates it, and run_numeric_extraction should be deleted -- it filters on v2_enriched_at and writes v2_extracted_values, v2_enrichment_version and v2_enriched_at, and none of those three columns exists on any table (checked against information_schema). It targets a four-column schema replaced by the v2_extracted_rules + v2_extraction_status pair. Found while removing it: get_enrichment_status() counted the same dead column, so `python enrichment/pipeline.py --phase status` raised UndefinedColumn on every invocation -- and two warning messages added yesterday (#1084) tell operators to run exactly that command when enrichment fails, so the instruction given at the moment something goes wrong pointed at a command that crashed. Standard rather than Critical: no production data is written or changed by this PR, and the deleted code could not execute.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_dead_numeric_phase_removed.py -q, plus the real layer PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest -m database tests/test_pipeline_status_real_db.py -q -o addopts=, and the command itself: python enrichment/pipeline.py --phase status
falsifiable_check.expected: 6 removal tests pass, 2 real-database tests pass, and --phase status exits 0 printing the corpus figures. Full suite 5,294 passed, 2 skipped.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: run_numeric_extraction is reintroduced, `--phase numeric` reappears as a command-line choice, any non-comment line in enrichment/pipeline.py references v2_enriched_at or v2_extracted_values or v2_enrichment_version, the status report stops returning a key the CLI prints, or the removed enriched/pending/enrichment_pct metrics come back.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Yes, forced both directions against the live database. Before the fix, `python enrichment/pipeline.py --phase status` exited 1 with psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column "v2_enriched_at" does not exist -- captured, not inferred. After the fix it exits 0. Then the dead column was re-inserted into the status query and the new real-database test was re-run: it went red naming the same UndefinedColumn, and the file was restored byte-identical (asserted in the harness). Without that second step the test would only prove the query runs today, not that it would catch the defect returning.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured live, read-only, before any edit. v2_extracted_rules is populated on 8,087 of 18,312 served rows and 18,222 of 59,519 overall; 100% of non-null values are jsonb ARRAYS, none objects. Correlation with v2_extraction_status is exact: complete 6,337 with rules of 6,337, review_needed 1,750 of 1,750, and all 10,225 null-status rows have none -- which only a single writer setting both columns in one UPDATE can produce. All writes date Jan-Mar 2026 (10,038 rows on 2026-01-27, last 2026-03-29); nothing for six months.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The plan assumed run_numeric_extraction was the thing that would populate v2_extracted_rules once fixed. It never wrote that column at all -- it writes v2_has_numeric_value, v2_extracted_values, v2_enrichment_version and v2_enriched_at. Three of those four exist nowhere in the database. The real writer is enrichment/rule_extraction_pipeline.py, which is the only code in the repo with a `SET v2_extracted_rules` besides scripts/_fix_980mm.py (a one-off repair of a single row, id 88235) and rollback SQL quoted in docs. Second mismatch, and the more useful finding: coverage is not spread across councils at all. Of the 8,087 served rows with rules, 7,268 are statewide (all statewide rows), 624 are city_of_sydney (all of its rows), and 195 are ku_ring_gai of 337. Ashfield, Marrickville, Leichhardt, Woollahra, Waverley and every other council have ZERO.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Pure deletion plus one repair. No new capability. The NumericExtractor class is NOT deleted -- it is used by rule_extraction_pipeline.py, by tests/test_numeric_extractor_unit_order.py and by about ten debug scripts; only the dead wrapper around it goes, along with the import that this change leaves unused.

functions.name: get_enrichment_status
functions.input: No arguments. Opens its own connection and runs one aggregate over regulatory_provisions.
functions.output: A dict of corpus counts. Three keys were REMOVED -- enriched, pending and enrichment_pct -- because they were computed from a count of v2_enriched_at, a column that exists on no table, which made the entire report raise rather than return.
functions.if_none: The removed metrics were deleted rather than repointed at a surviving column. Inventing a new definition of 'enriched' is choosing a value; deleting a metric that measured nothing only removes a claim, which is the safer of the two directions. The live coverage signals, site_condition_tagged and type_classified, were already in the same report and now read 44,898 of 44,898 after #1084.

values.name: columns run_numeric_extraction referenced
values.value: v2_enriched_at, v2_extracted_values, v2_enrichment_version -- none exists on any table; v2_has_numeric_value, the fourth, exists on regulatory_provisions and provision_versions
values.read_at: information_schema.columns, queried live 2026-09-11 for all six candidate names at once.
values.if_missing: Not applicable -- this IS the absence measurement, and it is the evidence for deleting rather than fixing.
values.why: Three of four columns absent means the function targets a replaced schema, not a broken query. Repointing it at the pair that replaced them would create a second writer for a field enrichment/rule_extraction_pipeline.py already owns.

values.name: v2_extracted_rules coverage
values.value: 8,087 of 18,312 served rows, but from only three sources: statewide 7,268, city_of_sydney 624, ku_ring_gai 195
values.why: Recorded because the plan describes this field as the differentiated asset. Every DCP council with deep coverage -- Ashfield, Marrickville, Leichhardt, Woollahra, Waverley -- has zero rows in it. That is a materially different picture from '44% covered' and is registered in the plan ledger.

queries.purpose: Counts corpus enrichment coverage for the status report that the commit and extract workers tell operators to run.
queries.where_clause: No WHERE clause by design -- it is a whole-corpus census, and every metric carries its own `CASE WHEN v2_is_actionable = true` filter inside the aggregate.
queries.why: The absent WHERE is deliberate and is why the DB-guard lint does not apply: this is a census over all rows, not a serving query. The defect was never a missing filter -- it was one CASE expression naming a column that does not exist, which made the whole statement raise.

break_it.scenario: Someone reintroduces run_numeric_extraction because the name reads like a phase that ought to exist.
break_it.what_happens: A test fails immediately and names the replacement to wire instead, rather than the function silently rejoining a sequence it cannot survive.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the absence is pinned by a test that explains what to use instead.
break_it.how: The comment above STANDARD_ENRICHMENT_PHASES records what it was and why it went, so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

break_it.scenario: A future edit adds another query referencing one of the three columns that do not exist.
break_it.what_happens: A source-level test fails, listing the offending lines, because comments may name those columns but code may not.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the check skips comment lines so the explanatory note does not fail its own explanation.
break_it.how: Scoped to enrichment/pipeline.py. The repo-wide gate for this class exists but does not cover this directory -- see residual_risk.

break_it.scenario: The status query is changed and quietly stops returning a key that the command-line printer reads.
break_it.what_happens: The real-database test fails naming the missing key, instead of --phase status trading an UndefinedColumn crash for a KeyError crash.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest -m database tests/test_pipeline_status_real_db.py -q -o addopts=
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: every key the CLI prints is asserted present.
break_it.how: Executing the query against the real catalog is the only way to catch this class -- a mocked psycopg2 answers a MagicMock to any column name.

break_it.scenario: The deleted enriched / pending / enrichment_pct metrics are restored against whichever column is convenient.
break_it.what_happens: The real-database test fails and says to define such a metric against a column that exists and to state which.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest -m database tests/test_pipeline_status_real_db.py::test_the_removed_metrics_are_really_gone -q -o addopts=
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: their absence is asserted, not merely assumed.
break_it.how: A coverage percentage computed from a column nobody writes is worse than no percentage, because it reads as measured.

break_it.scenario: NumericExtractor is deleted too, on the assumption it went with its wrapper.
break_it.what_happens: A test fails: the class is imported by rule_extraction_pipeline, by a unit test of its own and by roughly ten debug scripts.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the confusable negative is pinned, so 'the tests pass' cannot mean 'everything numeric was removed'.
break_it.how: Only the dead wrapper and its now-unused import were removed.

break_it.scenario: An operator follows a runbook and runs the deleted command during a council onboarding.
break_it.what_happens: The three documents that instructed it now name the live path, enrichment.rule_extraction_pipeline, and say when and why the old phase went.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: docs updated in the same change that removed the command.
break_it.how: A fourth document, .claude/docs/LGA_EXTRACTION_RUNBOOK.md, already said 'Skip --phase numeric (v2_enriched_at column not in current DB schema)' -- the breakage was known and worked around rather than removed, which is why three other documents still pointed at it.

break_it.scenario: The module docstring keeps offering the deleted command as something to run.
break_it.what_happens: A test fails naming the line, so the most-read part of the file cannot go on documenting a command the parser no longer accepts.
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated: the docstring's Usage block is asserted, not just the argparse choices list.
break_it.how: Missed on the first pass and caught by a stray grep listing line 8 of the file itself: the choices test cannot see a docstring and the dead-column test skips prose, so between them the Usage block was uncovered. Both loosened tests were then forced red to confirm they still bite.

mutation_analysis: The change is a deletion, so the meaningful mutation is restoring what was deleted, and that was run against the live database rather than a mock: re-inserting the v2_enriched_at count into the status query turned tests/test_pipeline_status_real_db.py red with the original UndefinedColumn error, and the file was restored byte-identical afterwards (asserted in the harness). The five removal tests were additionally checked to be non-vacuous by confirming each names a specific symbol or line rather than asserting a count. Full suite green before and after: 5,293 passed, 2 skipped. Two further mutants after the docstring fix, both KILLED: re-advertising `--phase numeric` in the module Usage block, and returning a dead column to the status query. Both tests had just been narrowed to look at runnable code rather than any mention of the names -- an earlier version failed on its own explanation -- so confirming they still fail was the point.
residual_risk: 1) THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, found while doing this and deliberately NOT fixed: scripts/validate_schema_contract.py is the repo's gate for exactly this defect class -- 'every table and column referenced in code exists in the database', wired into CI as 'Schema contract (code vs live catalog)'. Its DEFAULT_ROOTS are only frontend-nextjs/app/api and services. It does not scan enrichment/ or scripts/, which is where most database-writing code lives, and is why v2_enriched_at survived there. Measured the cost of widening it rather than guessing: running it with --root enrichment --root scripts reports 54 INVALID references naming objects the database does not have. Widening the gate is therefore a 54-finding job of its own and belongs in its own PR; recorded in the plan ledger. 2) v2_extracted_rules is written by a pipeline invoked only from scripts/onboard_council.py -- not the commit path, not the extractor, not any cron -- and has not run since 2026-03-29. Whether it SHOULD run on a schedule is a product question this PR does not answer. 3) That pipeline selects all served rows without checking whether rules already exist, so a re-run overwrites rather than fills blanks. Not exercised here, but it means 'just re-run it' is not a safe instruction. 4) The three councils with rules are statewide, city_of_sydney and ku_ring_gai only; the deep-coverage DCP councils have none. This PR measures that and changes nothing about it.

post_merge.db_reset: None. This PR writes no data and changes no schema. The deleted code could not execute, so nothing that ran before stops running.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run `python enrichment/pipeline.py --phase status` and confirm it exits 0 and prints the corpus figures -- before this change it raised UndefinedColumn. Also confirm `python enrichment/pipeline.py --phase numeric` now errors as an invalid choice rather than crashing partway through a query.
